summary: Shipped a three-phase home-automation surface for myiotsan, entirely on top of its existing gated actuation path. Phase 1: `entities.ProfileCommand.Kind` gained five values beyond switch/setpoint -- dimmer/position (a 0..100 percentage), cct (a Kelvin setpoint bounded by min/max), mode (one of the integer values a new `options` field enumerates as a JSON [{value,label}] list, itself refusing an empty/unlisted value the same way an unbounded setpoint refuses everything), and color (an RGB colour packed into one integer, 0xRRGGBB, carried through the existing single-float DeviceCommand/twin model via new packRGB/unpackRGB helpers, with renderPayload substituting {r}/{g}/{b} into the command's payload template). Along the way, `services.validateValue`'s kind switch gained a `default` case that REFUSES an unrecognised Kind -- closing a latent hole where an unknown or misconfigured kind was previously published to a device completely unvalidated. A new builtin `smart-lamp` profile (Zigbee2MQTT conventions: power/brightness/color_temp/color) is the worked example. Phase 2: new `Scene`/`SceneAction` entities and `services.SceneService` group an ordered set of device commands under one name ("goodnight", "movie night") and run them via `POST /api/scenes/{id}/run` (admin-only) by fanning out through the exact same `CommandService.Issue` a manual command takes, one call per action -- every gate (actuation-enabled, admin-only, declared-commands-only, server-side bounds, rate limit, audit, twin confirmation, never-auto-retry) applies per action, and a scene never rolls back or stops early on a refusal, reporting each action's outcome independently (verified live: a scene run's per-action report correctly surfaced a rate-limit refusal on one action while the rest still succeeded). Phase 3: new `Schedule` entity and `services.ScheduleService` fire a scene or a single command at a fixed time of day (optionally weekday-filtered) or at local sunrise/sunset plus or minus an offset -- the sun times computed locally via a new pure NOAA sunrise/sunset calculation (`services/sun.go`, no network dependency, verified against published almanac times for London and the Svalbard midsummer polar-day case) against a site latitude/longitude stored as a runtime setting (`GET/PUT /api/settings/location`, admin-only). A new `safego.Supervise`d `myiotsan.scheduler` task ticks once a minute, aligned to the minute boundary, and fires every due schedule through the identical actuation path, with a persisted `LastFiredAt` unix-minute double-fire guard (the same restart-survives-cooldown discipline IotRule's alert cooldown already applies, now applied to time) and a synthetic `schedule:<name>` firing actor so the audit trail attributes it rather than reading "System". New RBAC rows: /api/scenes and /api/schedules are readable by viewer/operator; running a scene, test-firing or authoring a schedule, and setting the site location are all admin-only, mirroring the line issuing a command already draws. Frontend gained a Scenes page and a Schedules page (schedule editor plus a location panel) under a new Automation nav group, plus slider/select/colour-picker widgets on the device Control tab for the new command kinds. Verified live end to end: booted the app, seeded smart-lamp, issued a dimmer command, ran a scene, set the site location, and created and test-fired a sunset schedule.
compatibility: No behavior change for any existing device, profile, scene-free or schedule-free install: the new Kind values, the Options field, and the two new entities/tables are additive, and the only existing profile with any declared command (smart-relay) is untouched. An existing switch/setpoint command continues to validate and render exactly as before. The closed default-case hole in validateValue cannot regress a previously-working command -- every shipped profile before this change declared only switch/setpoint, both of which already had explicit cases. Scenes and schedules ship with zero rows on every existing install; nothing runs automatically until an admin creates one. Rule-driven actuation (an IotRule triggering a scene or command automatically, with no human in the loop) is deliberately NOT built here and is explicitly deferred to a later, security-reviewed change -- see docs/MYIOTSAN_PLAN.md section 8h.
